A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPC research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support comparison, including the new Appendix B.4 in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original GNN training and evaluation results, including accuracy, average precision and Monte Carlo estimates of MPC on synthetic and real-world graphs.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and simulations in Section 5 and Appendix D. Retained results establish original empirical content despite the absence of new experiments.

M1.justification: New Appendix B.4 sketches a temporal adaptation that evaluates MPC on transformed graph snapshots, producing time-dependent complexity scores. The existing lossyWL updates, static MPC procedure and Monte Carlo algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same information-retention, information-propagation and ring-transfer tasks on random regular, Erdős–Rényi, peptide and ZINC graphs, and retain the same WL-hash datasets. Temporal graphs are discussed prospectively without new training or evaluation.

E2.justification: WLC remains the complexity baseline. Corresponding experiments retain MLP, GraphSage, GCN, GIN, GCN-VN, GSN, FragNet, CIN, GAT and GATv2, including the comparisons in Figures 9, 14 and 18.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the same graph generation, dataset sizes, splits, metrics, model depths, learning rate and 50-epoch training limit. The added statement identifying FragNet's GCN backbone discloses an existing setting rather than reporting a setting replacement.

E4.justification: The hidden-dimension and graph-degree sensitivity analyses, sample-size studies and tests across graph families are retained with identical plots. The expanded Appendix D overview summarizes existing analyses rather than adding evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 still reports averaging results over three training seeds. The shaded bands in result plots and other statistical reporting are unchanged; no new run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all corresponding result plots retain their values and trends. For example, Table 2 reports the same ZINC MAE values of 0.37 for GCN, 0.078 for FragNet and 0.077 for CIN. The revised GSN inequality is a theoretical-bound change.

T1.justification: The GSN upper bound in Lemmas 5.3 and C.13 changes from (s/2) log(r+1) to ceil(s/2) log(r+1), with matching proof revisions. The FragNet proof corrects the destination from u to v. Definition 4.4 explicitly states the finite-seed condition already used in Appendix C, and Appendix B.4 adds a time-indexed MPC definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: MPC captures task-specific message-passing difficulty, preserves expressivity impossibility results and explains empirical behavior through architectural alignment. The temporal sketch does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 newly discusses temporal applicability and studying how task complexity evolves as the underlying graph changes. Existing interpretations of experimental results and limitations concerning optimization, attention, unknown target functions and complexity computation remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation-access link in the introduction's footnote and specifies in Appendix D.1 that its FragNet implementation uses GCN as the base MPNN. These improve access instructions and implementation disclosure; the PDFs do not establish a changed implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Longa et al.'s survey of temporal graph neural networks as reference 34 to support Appendix B.4. Existing research positioning remains substantially intact; most other citation changes are renumbering or additional references to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, condenses parts of Section 6 and Appendix A, adds subsection B.4 and expands the Appendix D overview. Section order remains intact, and the first-page footer changes from a preprint notice to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: The figure images and table contents are retained. Captions for Figures 1, 2 and 6 receive limited edits, Figure 6 is slightly resized, and float placement changes, notably moving Figure 10 onto a separate page.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility documentation through implementation-access information and the disclosed FragNet backbone. It also clarifies formal assumptions and corrects proof details while adding a limited temporal extension. These gains improve precision and usability, but the empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
